title: Android Battery Draining Fast? What to Check, in Order
html:
When an Android battery drains too fast, work out which of three things is responsible: one app, the screen and settings, or an ageing battery. Open Battery usage first. It tells you which one to chase. Then limit the app, change the screen settings, and only then look at the battery itself.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Menu names differ between brands; the Settings search box finds them.

I checked the battery screens on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 10 Oct 2026.

First, note a baseline

Write down how much battery you lose in a normal hour of use, and how long the screen was on. Without that number you cannot tell whether a change helped.

1. Restart and update. A little extra drain after an update is normal

Restart the phone, then check for updates in Settings, then System, then Software update. Update your apps in the Play Store (profile picture, Manage apps and device). Google's Pixel help also notes that right after a software update the battery can drain a bit more than usual, because the phone is downloading and optimising the new software. Give it a day before you judge.

2. Find what is using the battery

Go to Settings, then Battery, then Battery usage, and view it by apps. The top of the list is where your battery goes. Ask whether each entry makes sense. A game you played for two hours should be there. A shopping app you opened for a minute should not be.

If an entry like "Android System" or "Google Play services" sits at the top, you cannot sensibly switch it off. Update the phone and your apps first, and look at what else changed around the same time, such as a new app, a weak mobile signal, or a sync that is stuck.

3. Limit the app that is draining it

Open Settings, then Apps, tap the app, then App battery usage, then Allow background usage. Keep it on Optimized for most apps, as Google recommends. Use Restricted only for an app that keeps showing up as a heavy user and that you do not need to deliver messages instantly.

Google also warns that if you turn off battery optimisation for an app, it can run more while you are not using it and use more battery than needed. Adaptive Battery, found under Settings, then Battery, then Battery Saver, learns which apps you use less often and lets them run less.

4. The screen and a few features

Google's list of the biggest levers is short: lower the brightness, turn on the dark theme, shorten the screen timeout (Settings, then Display), turn off the Always-on display, and switch off live wallpapers. Tethering and hotspots also use a lot of power while they are on.

5. Battery Saver for when you need it

Settings, then Battery, then Battery Saver. Google says it reduces performance and limits background activity to make the battery last longer. You do not need a separate "battery saver" app for this: it is built in.

6. Is the battery itself getting old?

If the battery drains fast even with a light load, and it has been used for a couple of years, the battery may be worn. How to check depends on the phone.

  • Pixel 6 and later: Settings, then Battery, then Battery Diagnostics. Google says it can tell you when the battery needs replacing. If the battery icon shows a question mark, Google says to take the phone to an authorised repair centre.
  • Samsung Galaxy: the menu name changes between One UI versions, and I did not test a Samsung phone, so I am not giving a path here.
  • Other brands: menus differ and there is no single path that works for all. On my vivo V23 Pro (Funtouch OS 14) the path is Settings, then Battery. The screen starts with a chart under "Usage since last full charge", then shows Screen time and a list called "Power consumption rankings" with a "View by apps" drop-down. Each app in the list shows its screen time, its background time and its share of battery use in percent. I did not find a battery health figure on that screen.

Charging habits matter for how fast a battery ages. Pixel phones have Charging optimization under Settings, then Battery, then Battery health, with Adaptive Charging and a "Limit to 80%" option. Samsung has Protect battery: when it is on, charging stops at 85% (it is off by default, and available only on some models and software versions). Settings, then Battery, then Protect battery.

If none of it helps

If the battery still drains fast after the steps above, and Battery usage shows no single heavy app, the battery is the likely cause. Ask an authorised service centre what a battery replacement costs, and compare that with what the phone is worth before you decide. If the phone also lags, read why your Android phone is slow, because the two often share a cause such as an app stuck in the background.

What to do next

  1. Note a baseline hour.
  2. Restart, update, and wait a day after a big update.
  3. Read Battery usage and limit the one app that stands out.
  4. Reduce brightness, screen timeout and Always-on display.
  5. Check battery health, and use a charge limit if your phone has one.
